Signals large potential liability avoidance or compensation; shapes PCG regulatory and valuation outlook.
Sets a higher asset valuation bar vs CCSF’s $3.4B, implying lower deal likelihood or higher proceeds.
Adds material non-asset costs that could deter a sale and protect remaining customers’ economics.
Further inflates transaction cost; complicates execution timeline and feasibility.
Frames political/customer headwinds to municipalization; reduces probability of takeover.

This is a regulatory-stage defense against municipalization, setting a high valuation bar after CCSF’s lower offer. A CPUC ruling or CCSF revision recognizing higher costs—or abandoning the bid—would turn this into a clearer catalyst.
